target_customer: Early-stage startups and their employees and HR leads who pay for live online training workshops
problem: Startup employees need practical training such as becoming a manager, working remotely and handling stress, and have little access to live interactive instruction.
business_model: marketplace take rate on live online workshops, also pitched as paid training to startup HR teams

founders.name: Brian Park
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder and CEO and gives no education or employers.

founders.name: Malea Gadoury
previous_startups: Describes herself on the YC page as a former startup founder (YC S20) and operator
founders.background_notes: YC page describes 18 years of UX experience, no employers or education named.

exit.reason: Cause not public; the YC directory marks the company Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace around live video sessions could be assembled from existing video and payment tooling by a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Workshops are supplied by hosts who can use any video tool, so there was little to stop hosts and buyers from going direct or to rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent reacting to Foreword; the company went inactive on its own, cause not public.

market_need_then: The 2020 shift to remote work created demand for online professional training; the founders wrote on Product Hunt that the topics were ones they wished they had help with at startups, such as management and remote work.

branding.domain_note: Used foreword.live rather than an exact .com; no source on how it was obtained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product Hunt post was candid and personal, admitting a windy journey with a pivot or two.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a Product Hunt listing with few followers turned up; no press or community about the brand. The word foreword is also a book term, which makes it easy to confuse in search.

outcome_analysis: Foreword ran a marketplace for live online workshops for startup professionals and went through the Summer 2020 batch with two founders. The only funding seen is a single database entry for a convertible note, and no shutdown post-mortem or press coverage exists, so the cause of going inactive is not public and failure factors are left empty. The Product Hunt post mentions a pivot or two before launch without dating them. Workshop marketplaces had low barriers and many incumbents, but no source ties the outcome to any of that.
notes: foreword.live did not resolve from this sandbox (DNS failure), so treated as possibly dead; not independently confirmed. The $500K convertible note rests on a single database (CB Insights) and its January 2020 date precedes the Summer 2020 batch, so the date is doubtful. No Form D or press release found. Pivot or two mentioned in the founders' Product Hunt post, undated. Competitors list left empty: only undated or much later pages found (CreativeLive founded 2009 per review pages, Maven live workshops are a later product). Cause of inactivity not public.
